title: Carolina Hurricanes sign Zach Sawchenko to one-year contract
text:
Carolina Hurricanes sign Zach Sawchenko to one-year contract
M. P. Welch
The Carolina Hurricanes announced on July 5 that goaltender Zach Sawchenko has been signed to a one-year, two-way contract. The deal will pay Sawchenko $850,000 if he plays in the National Hockey League or $150,000 in the American Hockey League, with a guaranteed minimum of $190,000.
General Manager Eric Tulsky confirmed the signing and outlined Sawchenko's recent performance. The Calgary native spent the 2025-26 season with the Cleveland Monsters in the AHL, recording a 14-10-3 record with a 3.05 goals-against average and an .880 save percentage. At age 28, Sawchenko has appeared in seven NHL games for the San Jose Sharks, where he registered a 1-2-1 record with a 3.35 goals-against average and .905 save percentage.
Sawchenko's professional career includes time with several AHL teams—San Jose, Abbotsford, Chicago and Cleveland—where he holds an overall record of 56-57-15 across 135 games and maintains a career goals-against average of 3.08 along with an .895 save percentage. He also played for Chicago during the Hurricanes’ affiliation in the 2022-23 season and posted a record of 17-18-3.
In addition to his AHL experience, Sawchenko has played in the ECHL for Orlando and Allen, going 13-4-3 over twenty games with a notable goals-against average of 2.42 and .928 save percentage. Before turning professional, he spent two seasons at the University of Alberta where he earned a combined record of 28-4-1 with five shutouts over thirty-four games.
Sawchenko also played junior hockey for Moose Jaw in the Western Hockey League across four seasons totaling eighty-eight wins out of one hundred seventy-seven appearances.
The Carolina Hurricanes have recognized significant contributors such as Eric Staal and Rod Brind'Amour by inducting them into their Hall of Fame following achievements like winning their first Stanley Cup championship in 2006, according to their official website. The team’s home venue is Raleigh’s Lenovo Center, which accommodates up to twenty thousand people and hosts more than one hundred fifty events each year while contributing over two hundred million dollars annually to the local economy through events and community engagement, according to its official website.
